subject: MockMLDSAVerifier

artifactManifest.notes: bytecodeHash is keccak256 of the live runtime bytecode with the decoded trailing solc CBOR metadata region (53 bytes total: a 2-byte length suffix plus a 51-byte CBOR map — see evidenceFile) zeroed out; executableBytecodeMatch covers this same normalized region. Of that 53-byte region, only 32 bytes actually differ between live and locally-built bytecode (the 32-byte sha256 digest inside the metadata's `ipfs` multihash) — every other byte in the region, including the `solc` version tag, is identical. MockMLDSAVerifier has no `immutable` variables and no constructor arguments, so no immutable-slot verification applies. All facts on this record (executableBytecodeMatch, metadataHashMatch, metadataTrailerBytesExcluded, bytecodeHash) are deterministically RE-DERIVED from evidenceFile by `npm run validate:reproducibility` every run (scripts/lib/reproducibility-evidence.ts) — not hand-asserted. The deployment-commit build in evidenceFile was compiled from a worktree pinned to the deployment commit (Hardhat 2 / solc 0.8.24+commit.e11b9ed9, optimizer runs=200, evmVersion=cancun) via a clean `npm ci` + `npx hardhat compile`; independently cross-checked with a second solc build variant (solc-js/WASM) to rule out a compiler-binary cause for the metadata divergence.

disclosures: TESTNET ONLY — Ethereum Sepolia. Research prototype. Not audited. No production security guarantee. Do not use real funds.

This is a MOCK verifier. It performs structural length/shape checks only — it does NOT verify a real ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204 / Dilithium3) lattice signature on-chain. A passing result means 'structurally plausible', never 'cryptographically authorized'. See docs/Verifier_Roadmap.md.

All executable runtime bytecode was independently recompiled from public commit 35c25fa294bebea44b3089aa2435a190a5adf3fb (tag v0.4.24) and matched the live Sepolia deployment exactly. Of the trailing 53-byte solc CBOR metadata region, 32 bytes differ (the metadata hash content, a non-executed IPFS content pointer never run by the EVM) — consistent with a build-environment difference (OS/toolchain/path) rather than a source or code difference; those 32 bytes are not claimed to match and do not affect on-chain behavior.
No Ethereum mainnet deployment of this contract exists or is planned.
